A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same syntactic-adaptation study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of Switchboard and generated GPT-4o conversations, including regression results, bootstrapped divergence trajectories, and an all-rules robustness analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original Llama-3-8B regression results, divergence trajectories, and corpus analyses.

M1.justification: The conversation-generation and adaptation-measurement procedures remain unchanged: persona prompting, cross-speaker rule sampling, mixed-effects regression, and splitwise Jensen-Shannon divergence. Llama is an additional studied model; the new sampling diagrams explain the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage remains Switchboard and English LLM conversations using the same 17 personas and the topic 'What makes a day a good day?'. The added Llama conversations vary the generating model within this retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The random-conversation control and Switchboard reference remain unchanged. Neither version evaluates alternative adaptation-analysis methods; Llama-3-8B is introduced as another study subject.

E3.justification: v2 adds Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct as an experimental configuration, retaining 135 of 136 persona-pair conversations and 513 of 520 agent-5/6 conversations. Existing GPT and human settings, including the 49%/2%/49% partition and 200-word trajectory splits, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix E and Figure 11 add qualitative examples of repetitive affirmation and farewell loops, clarifying failures previously mentioned without examples. The all-rules robustness analysis in Appendix D and Tables 2-3 is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report regression standard errors, z statistics, and p-values, and use 100 bootstrap resamples to report JSD means and standard deviations. v2 applies these existing reporting practices to Llama without changing them.

E6.justification: v2 adds a substantial set of Llama results: regression coefficients in Table 1, adaptation trajectories in Figure 3, and corpus statistics and persona-divergence values in Appendices B-C. Retained GPT and Switchboard regression values are unchanged. The new Llama effect is inconsistently reported: Table 1 gives SameConv beta = 0.505, while Section 4 lists 0.198 and 0.364 for the two models.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix E's probability derivation involving 1-(1-p)^2-p = p(1-p) and its monotonicity below p = 0.5. No replacement mathematical argument is supplied; the new parse-tree diagram illustrates existing concepts.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion extend the explicit demonstrated-adaptation claim from GPT-4o to GPT-4o and Llama-3-8B. The abstract's general claim and the central contribution concerning gradual adaptation during long conversations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the detailed interaction-effects interpretations in v1 Appendix E, including the proposed binary-encoding artifact and stochasticity explanation. It adds an explicit limitation concerning transfer to human-LLM conversations and revises model-generalization discussion, while retaining the main context-conditioning hypothesis and binary-measure sensitivity limitation.

D1.justification: v1 promises dataset release upon acceptance; v2 states that code and data are public and provides a repository link. v2 also specifies Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct and approximately seven GPU hours on one NVIDIA H100. Existing prompt and parser details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Grattafiori et al. (2024), The Llama 3 Herd of Models, and removes the description of Cai et al. as the only prior adaptation study. The positioning around extending short-term priming research to long conversations remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and broad section sequence are retained, with localized rewrites of sampling, bootstrapping, discussion, and limitations. v2 adds Acknowledgements and replaces the interaction-effects appendix with a repetition-pattern appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds parse-tree and sampling diagrams, three Llama appendix plots, and repetition examples. Table 1 expands to three corpora, and the original trajectory chart becomes a paired-model chart with a zero-based axis. Existing appendix figures are resized, relocated, and recaptioned; Figure 7 introduces an erroneous Llama title within the GPT plot.

improvement.justification: The Llama replication broadens empirical support beyond v1's GPT-only evidence, while sampling diagrams and documented code/data access improve clarity and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the inconsistent new Llama coefficient and the mislabeled panel in Figure 7. The qualitative adaptation finding gains support, but precise reporting remains imperfect.
